Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, the fish-control transfer instructions, and the required wake-visual inspection workflow. Then I’ll inspect the inherited and sampled rollout evidence before proposing or editing the single candidate.

The workspace requires two skills here. I’m using the wake-visual skill to compare the best finite rollout with the most informative failure across both image rows, and the explicitly requested bookshelf skill to translate only a compact control invariant—not published gains or trajectories—after that evidence is understood.

All four rollouts confirm direct uniform still-water initialization, so the visual evidence is admissible. The sampled set contains no capture: the strongest trajectory improves distance by about 3.19 L before exiting upward, while the clearest failure moves farther from the target. I’m now comparing those two sheets from release through termination and will cross-check the apparent motion against their detailed state/force traces.

The visual and trace comparison isolates a useful result: posterior-only target curvature preserved strong propulsion and improved progress, but every first-generation curvature variant still crossed into negative bearing and exited the upper boundary. Moving the oscillator’s head center nearly removed the acceleration clipping, yet also collapsed useful travel. I’m consulting the bookshelf now for a compact mechanism that adds corrective course stability without repeating the failed head-centering architecture.

The bookshelf mechanism I’m carrying forward is half-cycle amplitude asymmetry: keep the proven joint-state traveling wave, but strengthen only the tail half-cycle that bends toward the target and weaken the opposite half-cycle. This directly addresses the evidence that a static posterior offset helped progress yet could not arrest the centerline overshoot; it also avoids moving the head oscillator’s center, which the sampled failure showed can suppress propulsion. I’ll record that hypothesis and its falsification boundary before changing the candidate, as required by the visual-inspection skill.

The policy now contains exactly one architecture change relative to the parent: static posterior curvature is replaced by smooth, bounded half-cycle tail asymmetry, while the anterior carrier and target-error preprocessing stay fixed. I’m updating durable guidance with the sampled negative boundary—static offset variants improved distance but never recovered course, and anterior center bias destroyed useful propulsion—without claiming any outcome for this unevaluated candidate.

The candidate and both required evidence files are now updated. I’m invoking the prescribed non-CFD check runner to verify the semantic guidance change, policy contract and parameter schema, reflection/finite behavior, and the single editable solver boundary.

The prescribed check-runner could not start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable in this account—the same infrastructure limitation recorded by the parent worker. I have still invoked it as required; I’ll now execute its three exact non-CFD checks locally, separately, and repair any failure before finishing.

The first check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice, so the checker sees two parents before it can assess the guidance change. I’m removing only that duplicate marker, as the inherited workers did for the same checker condition, then rerunning the semantic check.

The semantic check passes. The Julia contract command is currently blocked by the environment rather than the policy: no `julia` executable is on `PATH` (the login shell also emits unrelated missing-SSH-directory setup warnings). I’ll locate any workspace/runtime Julia binary and, if none exists, use the repository’s deterministic schema/boundary checks plus a language-independent numerical reflection check so this remains non-CFD.

All available non-CFD checks now pass: the guidance update is materially different from the assigned parent, the solver boundary contains only the allowed candidate change, every `params.FIELD` is defined and active, and a 3,240-state numerical grid confirms finite outputs, reflection equivariance, positive scale bounds, bounded tail targets, and correctly signed cycle-mean steering. The only unavailable check is direct Julia execution because this environment has no Julia binary. I’m doing a final file audit now; no CFD will be run.

Completed one multi-wake policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) adds bounded, phase-aware half-cycle tail asymmetry while preserving the anterior oscillator.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:37) adds the reusable negative lesson from all four sampled curvature controllers.

Guidance semantics, parameter schema, solver boundary, finite-output grid, bounds, and reflection equivariance pass. The configured check-runner was invoked but its pinned model was unavailable; direct Julia execution was also unavailable because Julia is not installed. No CFD was run.
